title: 国際協力銀行と3メガバンク、3500億円の融資契約　対米投資第1弾で
extracted_text:
国際協力銀行（JBIC）は1日、日米関税交渉で合意した対米投融資の第1弾として、3案件向けに民間銀行との合計で約3500億円を上限とする融資契約を結んだと発表した。資金集めの枠組みが固まり、事業総額が5兆5000億円を超す巨大プロジェクトが始動する。

日米両政府は2月、第1弾として①中西部オハイオ州のガス火力発電所②南部テキサス州の原油積み出し港③南部ジョージア州の人工ダイヤモンド製造施設――と3つの開発案件を決めた。事業規模はそれぞれ5.2兆円、3300億円、900億円を掲げた。

政府系のJBICと三菱UFJ銀行、三井住友銀行、みずほ銀行の民間3行が協調融資するとみられる。事業ごとに設立した特別目的事業体（SPV）に貸し出す。工期が進んで新たな資金需要が発生するごとに融資を積み増す。

JBICと3メガ銀合計の融資の比率は各事業とも1対2とした。3メガ銀の拠出分には政府系機関の日本貿易保険（NEXI）が融資保証を付け、損失リスクを抑える。今回公表した融資契約額には保険料などの諸費用も含めた。

トランプ米政権による関税引き上げ表明を受けた交渉の結果、日米両政府は2025年7月に日本が米国へ5500億ドル（約84兆円）を投資する合意を結んだ。

第1弾で最大プロジェクトとなるガス火力発電所は、 ソフトバンクグループ が建設を主導するデータセンターへの電力供給を想定する。今回決まった融資契約の上限額は約3000億円に達した。東芝や 日立製作所 、 三菱電機 など日本の製造大手も参加する見通しだ。

規模で次点となるのが、テキサス州での原油積み出し港だ。米南部で産出するシェールオイルの輸出拠点となる想定で、中東情勢の悪化によって不安定になる世界の原油市場にとっても重要度が増す。協調融資の規模は最大500億円程度となった。

自動車部品や半導体の加工に用いる人工ダイヤは中国への依存度が高く、経済安全保障上の懸念が強まる。日米による安定供給に向けて40億円弱の融資が決まった。

日米両政府は3月、対米投資の第2弾を公表した。日本は小型原子力発電所や天然ガス火力発電設備の整備に最大730億ドルの資金を投じる。第1弾と並行して官民で融資交渉を進める。
translated_text:
JBIC announced on the 1st that it has finalized financing agreements with private banks for up to approximately 3.5 trillion yen across three projects, representing the first tranche of US investment and financing agreed upon during Japan-US tariff talks. With the funding framework now in place, a massive project with a total investment exceeding 5.5 trillion yen is kicking off.
In February, the two governments selected three development projects for the first tranche: a gas-fired power plant in Ohio in the Midwest, a crude oil export terminal in Texas in the South, and a synthetic diamond manufacturing facility in Georgia in the South. The scales were set at 5.2 trillion yen, 330 billion yen, and 90 billion yen, respectively.
Government-affiliated JBIC is expected to co-financed alongside the three private banks—MUFG Bank, SMBC, and Mizuho Bank. Loans will be extended to special purpose vehicles established for each project, with additional financing provided as construction progresses and new funding needs arise.
The financing ratio between JBIC and the three megabanks has been set at 1-to-2 for each project. Japan's trade insurance agency NEXI will provide loan guarantees for the megabanks' portions, reducing the risk of losses. The announced financing amounts include insurance premiums and other associated costs.
Following negotiations in response to the Trump administration's tariff hike announcements, the two governments reached an agreement in July 2025 for Japan to invest $550 billion into the US.
The gas-fired power plant—the largest project in the first tranche—is intended to supply electricity to data centers that SoftBank Group will lead in constructing. The ceiling for the financing agreement set for this project reaches approximately 300 billion yen. Major Japanese manufacturers including Toshiba, Hitachi, and Mitsubishi Electric are expected to participate.
The second-largest project by scale is the crude oil export terminal in Texas. It is planned as an export hub for shale oil produced in the US South, making it increasingly important given the instability of global crude markets due to the deteriorating Middle East situation. The coordinated financing is capped at around 50 billion yen.
Synthetic diamonds used in processing automotive parts and semiconductors have a high dependence on China, raising strong economic security concerns. Just under 4 billion yen in financing was agreed upon to ensure a stable supply by Japan and the US.
In March, the two governments announced the second tranche of US investment. Japan will invest up to $73 billion in the development of small-scale nuclear power plants and natural gas-fired power generation equipment. Financing negotiations will proceed on a government-private sector basis in parallel with the first tranche.
title_en: JBIC and Three Megabanks Sign 3.5 Trillion Yen Financing Agreement for First US Investment Tranche
